items.title: The average strongly held belief these days in AI has a half life of 6 months at best
items.text: The average strongly held belief these days in AI has a half life of 6 months at best. items.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
items.text: Over the past month, we’ve been looking into reports that Claude’s responses have worsened for some users. We’ve traced these reports to three separate changes that affected Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, and Claude Cowork. The API was not impacted. All three issues have now been resolved as of April 20 (v2.1.116). In this post, we explain what we found, what we fixed, and what we’ll do differently to ensure similar issues are much less likely to happen again. We take reports about degradation very seriously. We never intentionally degrade our models, and we were able to immediately confirm that our API and inference layer were unaffected. items.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
items.text: Get started with Claude Managed Agents by following our docs . A running topic on the Engineering Blog is how to build effective agents and design harnesses for long-running work . A common thread across this work is that harnesses encode assumptions about what Claude can’t do on its own. However, those assumptions need to be frequently questioned because they can go stale as models improve. As just one example, in prior work we found that Claude Sonnet 4.5 would wrap up tasks prematurely as it sensed its context limit approaching—a behavior sometimes called “context anxiety.” We addressed this by adding context resets to the harness. But when we used the same harness on Claude Opus 4.5, we found that the behavior was gone. The resets had become dead weight. We expect harnesses to continue evolving. So we built Managed Agents: a hosted service in the Claude Platform that runs long-horiz...

items.title: AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life
items.text: AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life. Here’s how to adapt. Most trad product teams are built to discover a playbook and then milk it for the next 5 years. However in the AI labs, we consciously throw away playbooks every few months cos we start seeing diminishing returns. Here’s what you can do as an AI builder: Focus on defining a set of meta-principles for 1/ how you continuously learn what the market wants today and what it might want in 3 months 2/ how you execute with extreme urgency The specifics of 1 and 2 will vary based on your domain and product type.
